title: Wavefunctions localization, and the Wigner's Friend Paradox in a Framework of Discrete-Space Hypothesis
abstract: We present a resolution of the Wigner's Friend paradox within a framework of quantum mechanics (QM) on the hybrid space RxQ_{p}, where Q_{p} denotes the field of p-adic numbers, regarded as a model of discrete microscopic space at the Planck-Bronstein scale. In this framework, wavefunction collapse is not an independent postulate but a dynamical consequence of the Schrödinger equation with non-local Hamiltonians: wavefunctions localize onto compact supports during measurement interactions, producing definite pointer readings without the intervention of observers or the exchange of information between subsystems. We model both Wigner and his Friend as classical apparatuses and show that each produces a definite reading through independent applications of the collapse mechanism, thereby eliminating the conflict between their descriptions of reality. The framework is consistent with the principal no-go theorems in finite- and infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces associated with extended Wigner's Friend scenarios -- including those of Frauchiger-Renner, Brukner, Bong et al., and Guérin et al. -- since it requires no agents capable of recording or reasoning about outcomes, thereby vacating the observer-dependent assumptions that drive those theorems. We illustrate the collapse mechanism explicitly through a toy model of a particle in a box, comparing the standard description with the new one. The non-locality intrinsic to QM on L2(RxQ_{p}) permits realism at the cost of locality, and the Absoluteness of Observed Events holds in our framework without requiring observer independence.
summary: This paper resolves the Wigner's Friend paradox by proposing that wavefunction collapse is a dynamical outcome of the Schrödinger equation when quantum mechanics is formulated on a hybrid space combining continuous ($\mathbb{R}$) and discrete ($p$-adic, $\mathbb{Q}_p$) dimensions. By modeling observers as classical apparatuses, it shows that definite measurement outcomes are absolute features of the dynamics, thus bypassing observer-dependent paradoxes.
main_problem: The paper aims to resolve the Wigner's Friend paradox by providing a quantum mechanical framework that eliminates observer-dependent assumptions.
main_result: It demonstrates that wavefunction collapse is a dynamical consequence of the Schrödinger equation on a hybrid space, leading to definite readings for all observers without requiring conscious agents or information exchange.
method: The authors construct a theory using Quantum Mechanics formulated on the product space $\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{Q}_p$, where $\mathbb{Q}_p$ models discrete microscopic space.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by quantum mechanics evolving on $L^2(\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{Q}_p)$, incorporating non-local Hamiltonians. The paradox is tested using toy models of particle measurement in both continuous and p-adic spaces.
key_observables: Wavefunction localization onto compact supports during measurement interactions, leading to definite pointer readings.
important_parameters: The structure of the $p$-adic numbers ($\mathbb{Q}_p$) at the Planck-Bronstein scale; non-locality vs. locality trade-off.
main_assumptions: The core assumption is that space at short distances is fundamentally discrete, modeled by $\mathbb{Q}_p$, and collapse emerges dynamically from the Schrödinger equation rather than being an independent postulate.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the hybrid space model, develops the dynamical mechanism for wavefunction localization via non-local Hamiltonians, applies this to resolve Wigner's Friend paradox by showing sequential, independent collapses, and concludes by demonstrating consistency with existing no-go theorems.
why_interesting: This work tackles foundational issues in quantum measurement theory (the measurement problem) using advanced mathematical structures ($\mathbb{Q}_p$), which is highly relevant for theoretical physicists exploring the foundations of QM beyond standard continuous models.
